first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly matching the performance lever documented in memory_86 and memory_31. Both prior experiments showed durable lift from signup/onboarding simplification in self-serve and SMB cohorts. Verifying memory_86 (day 52 consolidation) will confirm the persistence and magnitude of onboarding completion improvements, and memory_73 will establish the baseline effectiveness of promotional pricing as an alternative, allowing confident prioritization. The current situation presents concurrent threats (competitor pricing pressure, activation decline, onboarding decline), but onboarding simplification directly addresses the measurable drop in an upstream conversion metric we've proven we can move. This preserves optionality: if the onboarding lift materializes, it may also improve activation downstream; if activation remains flat, promotional pricing remains available for next week's slot. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is lower priority this week because the immediate crisis is self-serve cohort performance, not pipeline quality. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers, not the onboarding/activation problems. One standard experiment (not over-broad rollout) maintains risk discipline while testing a high-confidence lever against a current headwind.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_86: onboarding simplification delivered +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. This is a durable, sustainable lever. Memory_73 archive reveals critical downside: the promotional pricing experiment achieved strong signup and qualified revenue lift (+31% signup, +18% qualified revenue) but destroyed retention (-12% at 30 days) and failed to sustain through renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing despite short-term competitive pressure; chasing price-sensitive cohorts with unsustainable discounting would harm long-term qualified revenue, our stated objective. Onboarding simplification directly addresses the 4% QoQ completion decline with proven sustainable mechanics (retention actually improved +3%). This experiment will improve upstream conversion, likely improving activation outcomes downstream without deploying a retention-destructive tactic. The competitor's aggressive pricing is a real threat, but responding in-kind with retention-negative discounting would lose the war while appearing to win individual skirmishes. Simplified onboarding rebuilds self-serve momentum defensibly.
